clue.text: Is one waiting around wanting to go Greek?

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the phrase for waiting is split open and goes around the clue's opening word

parts.note: something kept on ice is held in reserve, waiting
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about someone hanging about who longs to adopt Greek ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts IS inside ON ICE (waiting), giving ONICISE after the I for one. 'wanting to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something Ionic in style is to give it a Greek character, so the verb means to go Greek.

clue.text: A little socialist minnow to stab peer

definitions.meaning: someone mildly left-wing, a shade short of red
a dialect name for a small fish, the minnow or young salmon
an old verb meaning to pierce or prick with a blade
a dialect verb meaning to peep or peer with half-shut eyes

explanation.surface: A tiny fish with mild left-wing views tries to knife a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: Four separate definitions run together; 'peer' looks like a noun (a lord) but is the verb to peep.
explanation.definitionFit: Each phrase is a separate dictionary sense of the same short word: a mild leftie, a small fish, to pierce, and to peep.

clue.text: Violet Elizabeth's drunk orange consumable so?

definitions.meaning: Violet Elizabeth Bott, the lisping girl in Richmal Crompton's Just William stories, would say 'pissed' (drunk) with a lisp
an orange is made easy to eat by having its white inner rind taken off

explanation.surface: A puzzling picture of a lisping schoolgirl, the worse for wear, with an orange ready to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet Elizabeth Bott is the lisping little girl in the Just William books, so in her mouth 'pissed' (British slang for drunk) comes out with TH for SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the pith readies an orange for eating, and the lisped slang word for intoxicated has the same spelling.

clue.text: Devious man's divided existence in one body

indicators.note: the word for existence is split apart to take the other letters in its middle

parts.note: esse is Latin for being, used in English for existence

indicators.note: something devious takes a winding course, so the letters of man's wander into a new order

parts.note: the word man, with 's standing for has

explanation.surface: A cunning man leads a split life while pretending to be all of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of man's stands for 'has'; esse is the philosophers' Latin for existence.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is used in English for all together, as a single group or body.

clue.text: Embarrassed Tory fighting independent holding system

indicators.note: being embarrassed throws the letters of the politician's label into confusion

parts.note: fighting is war

explanation.surface: A red-faced Conservative clashes with an independent candidate over the way things are run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embarrassed' rearranges TORY to RYOT, itself an Indian word for a peasant farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the British Indian scheme of land tenure in which each farmer held land directly from the state, a landholding arrangement.

clue.text: Tragic agent not just brought up to keep pub free of drugs

indicators.note: to keep means to hold the next item inside
in a down clue, bringing something up turns it to read from bottom to top
not tells us to drop the word that follows from the agent's number

parts.note: the famous agent is 007, written out as double-O seven
just means even, as in an even or fair deal
PH is the map abbreviation for public house
someone off drugs is clean

explanation.surface: An undercover agent, rather unfairly raised, is told to keep a bar drug-free.
explanation.walkthrough: The agent is James Bond, 007, spelt out in letters; 'not just' leaves OOS, which 'brought up' turns to SOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to Sophocles, the Athenian dramatist of tragedies such as Oedipus, so it can mean tragic in style.

clue.text: Respect on cracking time!

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the little word goes inside the unit of time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

explanation.surface: An exclamation of approval for someone who is right on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem or high regard, as in 'to do someone the honour', is a synonym of respect.

clue.text: Round here in Nice, a rocker is a reasonable chap

indicators.note: round says the rocker goes around the French word

parts.note: a logan is a rocking stone, a boulder balanced so it rocks
ici is French for here, Nice being a French city

explanation.surface: A rock musician hanging round the Riviera turns out to be a sensible fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rocker' is not a musician but a logan, a balanced rocking stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone versed in logic is a person who reasons, a rational fellow.

clue.text: Anyone out there a solver who's talked about?

indicators.note: talked about tells us the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: the solver is the one addressed by the clue: you; the question word who, with 's as is

explanation.surface: Someone calls out to see whether anyone is there, and who is being discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, YOU and WHO run together into the call; the 's of 'who's' is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The call is the cry someone gives to attract attention or check whether anybody is present.

clue.text: Shilling given to kind QC

parts.note: S is the old abbreviation for a shilling, a former British coin
ilk means kind or sort

explanation.surface: A shilling handed to a type of barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: A QC is a Queen's Counsel, a senior British barrister, who 'takes silk' on appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior barristers wear gowns of this fabric, so the material is used as a name for a King's or Queen's Counsel.

clue.text: Pick up consumption by virtue of punching idol

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it

indicators.note: punching means driving into, so the shortened word goes inside the disease abbreviation

parts.note: consumption is the old name for tuberculosis, TB
thro is the shortened form of through, meaning by virtue of

explanation.surface: Catch a disease thanks to hitting a statue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up idol is a person whom fans swoon over, an object of romantic adoration.

clue.text: Cried recalling autodidactic course at Oxford, for one's admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let inside, so the degree course goes into the turned-round letters
recalling means calling back, so the abbreviation runs backwards

parts.note: self-taught suggests do-it-yourself, DIY
PPE, Philosophy, Politics and Economics, is a degree course offered at Oxford and elsewhere

explanation.surface: Someone yelled when remembering a self-taught Oxford degree, being let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalling' gives YID; 'for one' marks Oxford as only one place offering the course.
explanation.definitionFit: To yelp or let out short high squeals, as a small dog does, is to cry out.

clue.text: Transmission theory accounting for rotary engines keeping in step

indicators.note: keeping in means holding inside, so the dance step surrounds the jumbled letters

parts.note: pas is a step in ballet

indicators.note: rotary means turning round, so the letters are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: A theory to explain rotary engines that stay in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotary' makes NGENESI from the engines; 'accounting for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwin proposed this theory of heredity, in which every cell sends particles to the reproductive cells, a theory of how traits pass on.

clue.text: Getting round? This variety of crustacean's not cut out for it

definitions.text: Getting round? This variety of crustacean's not cut out for it

indicators.note: a variety is a different arrangement, so the pooled letters are reshuffled

parts.note: a round shape stands for the letter O
taken as written, the word crustacean

explanation.surface: A shellfish that stays put is plainly unsuited to travelling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not cut' means take C, U, T out of CRUSTACEAN with O added, leaving letters that rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This barnacle is a crustacean that fixes itself to rocks for life, so it is indeed not built for getting about.

clue.text: Housewife's sixth sense tingling on female poverty

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the preceding item
tingling suggests the letters are stirred up and rearranged
sixth picks out the letter at position six of the word

explanation.surface: A homemaker's intuition is tingling about a woman's hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tingling' gives EWNESS; poverty here is scarcity, not lack of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Poverty in its sense of scarcity or paucity means a small number, as in a poverty of ideas.

clue.text: Trap for fish caught in a group

indicators.note: in places the word for caught inside the group

parts.note: a set is a group
taken means caught or captured

explanation.surface: A fish trap that has caught a whole shoal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fishing net hung on stakes driven into a river or foreshore, a device for catching fish.

clue.text: Very tired, perhaps, cutting back plant

indicators.note: back tells us the whole assembly is read in reverse
cutting means slicing into, so the abbreviation goes inside the phrase for exhausted

parts.note: all in is slang for exhausted
eg, for example, is like perhaps in marking an instance

explanation.surface: Someone worn out cuts down a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts EG inside ALL IN for ALLEGIN, which 'back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Love-in-a-mist is the common name of this garden flower, a genus of annuals in the buttercup family.

clue.text: 26, say, right to have raised packing freight

indicators.note: packing means stuffing inside, so the freight holds the other letters

parts.note: a load is freight or cargo

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means turned to read upwards

parts.note: to own is to have

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another clue, with a right to lift freight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' gives NWOR; the clue at 26 is a French garden word, hence an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden term at 26 is borrowed straight from French, so it is an example of a word imported from another language.

clue.text: Himmler & co try to seize condemned tapes

indicators.note: to seize means to grab hold of, so the try surrounds the shuffled letters

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: condemned tapes are wrecked, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nazi chiefs attempt to grab incriminating recordings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condemned' turns TAPES into ESTAP, which GO surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinrich Himmler headed this Nazi secret police force, so he and his men are the organisation itself.

clue.text: Haunted by irrational fears, laid-back worker refined drug

indicators.note: being haunted means having something within, so the jumbled letters hold the insect
irrational suggests the letters are disordered
laid back means lying in reverse, so the worker is read backwards

parts.note: a worker bee is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A relaxed labourer tormented by phobias turns to purified narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irrational' gives FRASE and 'laid-back' gives EEB; 'laid-back' looks like a description of the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: This is cocaine purified from its salt for smoking, a refined form of the narcotic.

clue.text: Rack of ribs, English, delivered from Paris

indicators.note: to rack is to torture or wrench, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: A rack of ribs, cooked the English way, sent over from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rack' looks like a cut of meat but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The French call the English 'roast beef' as a teasing nickname, so it is what Parisians say for English people.

clue.text: Vulgar ______ cultivation = outrageous labour-saving?

indicators.note: outrageous means wildly out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of labour-saving
taken as written, the letters removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A line like a joke equation: vulgar cultivation equals outrageous labour-saving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageous' rearranges LABOURSAVING; take out the letters of VULGAR and BONSAI is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of growing miniature trees is a style of cultivation, filling the gap in the phrase.

clue.text: One may be writing about street wine-bar

indicators.note: about means around, so the pen goes round the street abbreviation

parts.note: a biro is a ballpoint pen, a thing used for writing

explanation.surface: Someone might be writing about a street of bars.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRO is the British everyday word for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A small informal restaurant serving wine and simple food is much like a wine bar.

clue.text: Top-class compiler returns to meet the lady escorts in dimly-lit area

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage
the lady is she

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: the compiler of a crossword is its setter

explanation.surface: A distinguished crossword setter goes back to meet a woman's chaperones in a darkened room.
explanation.definitionFit: These women showed cinema-goers to their seats by torchlight, guides in a darkened auditorium.

clue.text: China casing tungsten safety catch

indicators.note: casing means enclosing, so the friend wraps round the chemical symbol

parts.note: china is a mate or pal, from rhyming slang china plate
W is the chemical symbol for tungsten

explanation.surface: Porcelain wrapped round tungsten as a safety measure.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so china is a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: This pivoted bar engages a ratchet's teeth to stop it slipping back, a mechanical catch.

clue.text: Born to be subservient to half of mankind, I am

definitions.text: Born to be subservient to half of mankind, I am

indicators.note: in a down clue, being subservient means sitting below the preceding piece
half of means only one half of the word survives, here its second three letters

parts.note: people is mankind

explanation.surface: A low-born person laments being destined to serve others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' trims PEOPLE to PLE, and 'subservient to' puts B beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A commoner of low birth, destined to serve their betters, sums up the plebeian lot.

clue.text: Get in touch with London University about current capital

indicators.note: about means around, so the college's letters surround the next pair

parts.note: the LSE, London School of Economics, is part of London University
I is the symbol for electric current
capital means first-rate, A1, written here as AI

explanation.surface: Contacting a London college about money matters in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, first-rate, is read as the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as a link or go-between is to make contact and cooperate with someone.

clue.text: One goes about producing flower arrangement

parts.note: a parter is someone who parts, one who leaves
re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone moves around and creates a floral display.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a formal garden of flower beds laid out in a pattern, a horticultural arrangement.
